sidebar:

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

**Task:** keep a document that several people edit at the same time, where each
editor sends edits typed against the version it last saw.

One leader applies every edit in log order, so there is never a merge. The
problem is position: by the time "insert at 12" is applied, someone may have
typed before position 12. `Text` solves it the way collaborative editors do: it
is a [Fugue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00583) sequence in which every character
has a stable **id**. An insert names the id of the character it follows, a
delete names ids, so an edit lands where its author meant, and two runs typed
after the same character never interleave (`crates/sdk/src/collections/text.rs`).

## State

```rust
#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct Docs {
    body: Text,
    rich: RichText,
}
```

## Edit by id

The client keeps the ids it read (`chars()` returns `(id, char)` pairs) and
sends edits against them:

```rust
/// Inserts `text` after the character `after` (`None`: at the start); returns the new ids.
pub fn insert(&mut self, after: Option<u64>, text: String) -> app::Result<Vec<String>> {
    let ids = self.body.insert_after(after, &text)?;
    Ok(ids.iter().map(u64::to_string).collect())
}

/// Deletes the characters `ids`; ids already deleted are skipped, an id that never
/// existed is `UnknownId` and deletes nothing.
pub fn delete(&mut self, ids: Vec<String>) -> app::Result<u64> {
    let ids = ids
        .iter()
        .map(|id| id.parse::<u64>().map_err(|_| AppError::new("BadId")))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    Ok(self.body.delete_ids(&ids)?)
}
```

<Aside type="caution">
  The ids travel as strings: a `u64` inside a list (`Vec<u64>`) is refused at
  compile time, because it would lose precision in JavaScript (the D20 rule in
  [SDK macros](/core/build/sdk-macros/#applogic)). An `Option<u64>` on its own is
  a decimal string on the wire already.
</Aside>

`insert(index, str)` and `delete(index, n)` edit by position for a client that
holds the current text; `id_at(index)` and `index_of(id)` convert between the
two.

## Read

`read()` gives the text, `chars()` the characters with their ids, `len()` the
length in one read.

## Rich text

`RichText` is a `Text` plus marks: ranges with a key and an optional value
(bold, a link, a comment thread).

| Method | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `text()` / `text_mut()` | The underlying `Text`. |
| `mark(start, end, key, value, expand)` | Marks the range by position; `expand` makes it grow when text is typed at its end. |
| `mark_ids(..)` | The same by character ids. |
| `marks()` | The marks with their ids. |
| `spans()` | The text cut into spans, each with its attributes: what a renderer draws. |
| `clear()` | Removes the text and its marks. |

## Costs

Reads and edits load every node of the text, 1,000 per host read; `len` is one
read. Keep one `Text` per document rather than one large text for everything,
and use a table for document metadata.
